technique: 3D CGI rigged puppets styled to mimic stop-motion/claymation: skin and fabric have a felted, fibrous surface texture (visible fine grain on the man's jacket collar and the woman's sweater, and a matte pored texture on faces) and the character designs (elongated wedge noses, oversized round glasses, blocky felt coat) read as an Aardman/claymation pastiche. However, motion between adjacent periodic frames is fully continuous and pose-interpolated (smooth head turns, gradual torso rotation, per-word viseme changes) with no frame-doubling, popping, or fingerprint/seam artifacts typical of hand-manipulated clay or cutout puppets — so this is very likely CG (probably AI- or software-rigged 3D) animation dressed up in a stop-motion look rather than true physical stop-motion. Flagging uncertainty: without higher-frequency frames it's not fully verifiable whether the smoothness is native 30fps rendering or has been frame-interpolated in post.

The woman's brows and heavy-lidded eyes are similarly held in one droopy, skeptical expression across all her frames with only mouth movement layered on top.
eye_and_blink_notes: No blink was captured in any of the 15 periodic frames or 4 scene frames for either character, despite the frames spanning most of the clip's ~14s runtime — both leads appear to hold a fixed unblinking, wide-open-eyed stare (the man's eyes especially: bulging, static white sclera with pinprick pupils in every close-up). idle_motion_notes: Background elements are essentially static across all sampled frames: the curtains show no sway, the lamp's glow is constant, and the bedspread/pillow folds don't shift. Surface 'felt' texture on clothing stays fixed/noisy-but-static (no cloth-sim jiggle visible). The only ambient idle motion evident is the woman's hair bun, which shows very minor silhouette variation between periodic-9 and periodic-10, likely a secondary settle rather than deliberate animation.
frame_rate_feel: Metadata reports 30fps. Across the sampled periodic frames (roughly one per second) all pose, expression, and lip-sync changes look like smooth in-between interpolation rather than stepped/held frames — there's no visible stutter, doubled pose, or clay-fingerprint jitter typical of true stop-motion shot on 2s or 3s holds. The felt/clay surfacing suggests a stop-motion aesthetic, but the perceived motion itself feels like continuous CG animation running close to native frame rate.
overall_animation_style_notes: The short leans on a claymation/Aardman-pastiche character and material design (fibrous felt textures, exaggerated noses and glasses, blocky wool coats) layered over what behaves like clean, continuous CG animation with strong per-word lip-sync and held 'locked' brow expressions carrying most of the comedic tone. Big bold yellow serif title cards ('Episode 22', 'EXORCISM') and single-word-at-a-time animated captions are burned into the frame, and a costume/scene change (woman's black dress swapped for a brown sweater) marks a cut between the cold-open reveal and the dialogue scene.
